_provenance.asked: §36–§41: which closed routes exist in M9.2's real target-block graph, how many are 2-hop and 3-hop, which have every fee proved, whether two runs of one graph and one config agree byte for byte, and how much walking and how long that took — with every number recomputable from the raw run documents beside it by a reader who calls no production helper.
_provenance.endpoint_source: the digest of the endpoint M7 and M9.1/M9.2 recorded. This milestone makes no request at all: the graph is rebuilt from committed JSON, so the digest appears here only to keep the provenance chain unbroken, and no URL is written anywhere in this directory.
_provenance.written_at: the run, not the review: every count is read off the candidate rows beside it, and the one number that cannot repeat — the wall clock — lives in raw/ and is quoted rather than re-measured

fields.canonical_key: the route's least rotation, one `pool:token_in>token_out` per edge, joined by `+`
fields.edges: directed edges in trade order, identities only — no reserves, no amounts
fields.fee_status: `complete` only if every edge's pool has an attested fee; `incomplete` otherwise, and never a guessed rate
fields.start_token: the token spent first and received last, as the canonical rotation reads it
fields.target_block: the graph's target block, copied onto every candidate

ordering_rule: canonical_key ascending — the order the search returns, restated rather than re-sorted, so a reader can check the output arrived sorted (§25).
row_identity: §12: chain_id + target_block + the ordered edge sequence under canonical_key. No row position, no list index, no hash.
